1.reproduce_code:
---
title: "MWE"

format:
  pdf:
    documentclass: article
    pdf-engine: xelatex
    keep-tex: true
---

Figures

::: {#fig-elephants layout-ncol="2"}

![Surus](elephant.png)

![Hanno](elephant.png)

Famous Elephants
:::
```

To reproduce the issue, create a Quarto document with the above content and compile it to PDF. The subfigures will not have specific subfigure labels. To fix the issue, add cross-references to each subfigure as shown below:

```markdown
---
title: "MWE"

format:
  pdf:
    documentclass: article
    pdf-engine: xelatex
    keep-tex: true
---

Figures

::: {#fig-elephants layout-ncol="2"}

![Surus](elephant.png){#fig-surus}

![Hanno](elephant.png){#fig-hanno}

Famous Elephants
:::
```
1.explanation: The issue arises because the subfigures are not labeled with specific identifiers, causing them to be treated as regular figures. By adding cross-references (e.g., {#fig-surus} and {#fig-hanno}), Quarto generates the correct LaTeX code with subcaptions, allowing the subfigures to be labeled properly. The provided code snippets demonstrate both the problematic and the corrected versions.
1.bug_scenario: The bug scenario involves generating a PDF document using Quarto where subfigures are not labeled correctly when cross-references are not provided. In the initial example, subfigures are labeled as normal figures without specific subfigure labels. When cross-references are added, the subfigures are labeled correctly with subcaptions (a) and (b).
